title: FMGE PSM Day 4 Section 2
subject: Community Medicine
description: A 42-question PSM section from the reviewed Day 4 notes.

questions.stem: Which is the most commonly used measure of dispersion?
questions.explanation: Standard deviation (root-mean-square deviation) is the most commonly used measure of dispersion. Variance is its square and is less directly interpretable.

questions.stem: How is the data set 2, 3, 3, 5, 7, 9, 9 best described?
questions.explanation: The mode is the most frequent value. In this set, 3 and 9 each appear twice, so the data are bimodal.

questions.stem: Haemoglobin, which is normally distributed, is measured in the same 40 women before and after 12 weeks of iron supplementation. Which test compares the two sets of values?
questions.explanation: Normally distributed quantitative data from the same subjects measured twice call for the paired t-test.

questions.stem: For a 2 × 2 contingency table, what is the critical chi-square value at the 95% confidence level?
questions.explanation: A 2 × 2 table has 1 degree of freedom, and its critical χ² value at the 95% confidence level is 3.84.

questions.stem: A distribution has a mean of 42, a median of 35 and a mode of 30. The distribution is:
questions.explanation: Mean > median > mode indicates a right (positive) skew.

questions.stem: Haemoglobin values of 200 women, grouped into class intervals, are best presented as a:
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin is a continuous quantitative variable, and grouped continuous data are shown by a histogram. Bar charts, pie charts and pictograms display qualitative data.

questions.stem: Mean systolic blood pressure, which is normally distributed, is compared between 60 smokers and 60 non-smokers. Which test is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Comparing the means of a normally distributed variable between two independent groups needs the unpaired t-test.

questions.stem: An ogive is used to depict:
questions.explanation: An ogive is a cumulative frequency curve.

questions.stem: If the probability of a Type II error is 0.2, what is the power of the study?
A systematic sample of 50 households is drawn from a list of 1,000, and the random start is the 7th household. Which household is the third one selected?
questions.explanation: The sampling interval is 20, so the selected households are the 7th, 27th and 47th.

questions.stem: Which diagram best shows the incidence of malaria in a district over 15 years?
questions.explanation: A line chart shows the trend of a variable over time.

questions.stem: Which contraceptive approach has a Pearl Index of zero?
questions.explanation: Complete abstinence is the only approach with a Pearl Index of zero; every other method has some failure rate.

questions.stem: In simple random sampling, every unit of the population has:
options: A chance of selection proportional to its stratum's size
An equal and known chance of selection
A chance of selection determined by accessibility
A chance of selection only if it volunteers
questions.explanation: In simple random sampling, each unit has an equal and known chance of selection. Random-number tables are the preferred way to draw the sample.
questions.answer_label: An equal and known chance of selection
questions.answer: An equal and known chance of selection

questions.stem: After vasectomy, for about how long should the couple use another contraceptive method before semen analysis confirms sterility?
questions.explanation: After vasectomy, the couple should use a barrier or other method for about 3 months, until semen analysis confirms azoospermia.

questions.stem: What is the most common adverse effect of the three-monthly injectable contraceptive provided in India's public family-planning programme?
questions.explanation: The programme's three-monthly injectable is DMPA (Antara), whose most common adverse effect is irregular menstrual bleeding.

questions.stem: What is contraception used after unprotected intercourse called?
questions.explanation: Interceptive (postcoital or emergency) contraception is used after intercourse. Conventional contraceptives such as condoms and spermicides are used at the time of intercourse.

questions.stem: Which is an example of community participation in primary health care?
questions.explanation: Community participation is exemplified by ASHA and China's barefoot doctors. ORS, KMC and Shakir's tape are appropriate technologies.

questions.stem: Which spermicide is commonly used in contraceptive preparations?
questions.explanation: Nonoxynol-9 is the spermicide commonly used in contraceptive foams, creams and sponges. It damages the sperm membrane and acrosome.

questions.stem: Where is the multipurpose health worker (MPW) posted?
questions.explanation: The multipurpose worker is posted at the subcentre. ASHA works at village level and the Anganwadi worker at the Anganwadi centre.

questions.stem: The Billings method of contraception is also called the:
questions.explanation: The cervical mucus method is also called the Billings or ovulation method.

questions.stem: Which AYUSH system originated in Greece?
questions.explanation: Unani medicine is of Greek origin. Siddha and Sowa-Rigpa are of Indian origin.

questions.stem: The nonsteroidal oral contraceptive developed at CDRI Lucknow is contraindicated in:
questions.explanation: Ormeloxifene (centchroman) is contraindicated in polycystic ovarian disease.

questions.stem: Which progestogen does the combined oral contraceptive Mala-N contain?
questions.explanation: Mala-N contains levonorgestrel 150 mcg with ethinyl estradiol 30 mcg.

questions.stem: An arc welder with years of exposure to iron-oxide fumes has small, dense opacities on a chest X-ray but no functional impairment. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Iron-oxide exposure in welders causes siderosis, a benign pneumoconiosis with radiological opacities but little functional impairment.

questions.stem: ASHA was introduced under the:
questions.explanation: ASHA was introduced under the National Rural Health Mission in 2005.

questions.stem: A farmer develops fever, cough and breathlessness a few hours after handling mouldy hay. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Acute hypersensitivity pneumonitis after handling mouldy hay is farmer's lung.

questions.stem: What is free medical care provided to the population by the government called?
questions.explanation: State medicine means medical care provided free by the government.

questions.stem: Where did the system of medicine based on the principle "similia similibus curentur" originate?
questions.explanation: The principle "like cures like" belongs to homeopathy, founded by Samuel Hahnemann in Germany.

questions.stem: A furniture worker who has been exposed to hardwood dust for years is at increased risk of:
questions.explanation: Wood dust, like nickel and chromium, is linked to cancer of the nose and paranasal sinuses.

questions.stem: Which pneumoconiosis is caused by inhaling coal dust?
questions.explanation: Inhaling coal dust causes anthracosis (coal workers' pneumoconiosis).

questions.stem: Periodic medical examination of workers exposed to benzene is which level of prevention?
questions.explanation: Periodic examination of exposed workers aims at early detection, so it is secondary prevention.

questions.stem: Occupational exposure to radon in underground miners is linked to:
questions.explanation: Radon exposure in miners is a recognised cause of lung cancer.

questions.stem: A worker in a sugarcane-processing unit develops hypersensitivity pneumonitis after handling stored fibrous residue. Which organism is implicated?
questions.explanation: Exposure to stored sugarcane bagasse causes bagassosis, due to Thermoactinomyces sacchari.

questions.stem: All of the following are demographic processes EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Demography studies fertility, marriage, mortality, migration and social mobility. Morbidity is a health measure, not a demographic process.

questions.stem: Bird-fancier's lung results from exposure to:
questions.explanation: Bird-fancier's lung is hypersensitivity pneumonitis caused by avian proteins in bird droppings.

questions.stem: What is the movement of people from one social class to another called?
questions.explanation: Social mobility is movement between social classes, whereas migration is physical movement from one place to another.

questions.stem: In which stage of the demographic cycle does the death rate exceed the birth rate?
questions.explanation: In the declining stage, the death rate exceeds the birth rate, so the population falls.

questions.stem: In India, the child sex ratio is calculated for which age group?
questions.explanation: Child sex ratio = females aged 0–6 years / males aged 0–6 years × 1000.

questions.stem: In India, the census is conducted under the Ministry of:
questions.explanation: The Indian census is conducted every 10 years under the Ministry of Home Affairs, through the Registrar General and Census Commissioner.

questions.stem: A town had 48,000 people on 1 January and 50,000 on 1 July, and recorded 400 deaths during the year. What is its crude death rate per 1,000 population?
questions.explanation: CDR = deaths / mid-year population × 1,000 = 400 / 50,000 × 1,000 = 8.0.

questions.stem: What is the denominator of the child–woman ratio?
questions.explanation: Child–woman ratio = children aged 0–4 years / women aged 15–49 years × 1000.

questions.stem: How often is the independent retrospective survey of the Sample Registration System carried out?
questions.explanation: In SRS, continuous enumeration is cross-checked by an independent survey every 6 months. This dual record makes it the most accurate source of vital rates.
